note: OWASP publishes the Top 10 every few years, not every year. The recent lists are 2017, 2021 and 2025. There is no 2022, 2023 or 2024 list. CWE lists are the notable or typical ones, not the full mapping. Examples are minimal Python snippets for illustration.

lists.status: Official final release. owasp.org/Top10/2025 and the OWASP/Top10 GitHub README list it as released (Final) and mark 2021 as superseded. It went through alpha and release-candidate stages first.

categories.name: Broken Access Control
categories.description: Still #1. Users act outside their permissions. SSRF was folded into this category in 2025.

categories.name: Security Misconfiguration
categories.description: Up from #5. Systems, apps or cloud services set up insecurely: debug on, default credentials, open storage, risky XML parser settings.
categories.fixed_example:
app.config['DEBUG'] = False
ADMIN_PASSWORD = os.environ['ADMIN_PASSWORD']

categories.name: Software Supply Chain Failures
categories.description: New name and wider scope than 2021's Vulnerable and Outdated Components: compromised or vulnerable dependencies, build systems and distribution.
categories.fixed_example:
# requirements: pin a patched version and scan dependencies in CI
log4j-core==2.17.1

categories.name: Cryptographic Failures
categories.description: Down from #2. Missing or weak encryption, bad key handling, weak randomness.
categories.fixed_example:
import bcrypt
h = bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt())

categories.name: Injection
categories.description: Down from #3. Untrusted input reaches an interpreter, from cross-site scripting to SQL injection.
categories.vulnerable_example: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'")
categories.fixed_example: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s", (name,))

categories.name: Insecure Design
categories.description: Down from #4. Design and architecture flaws, including business logic, missing threat modeling and secure design patterns.

categories.name: Authentication Failures
categories.description: Renamed from Identification and Authentication Failures. Weak login, credential or session handling.
categories.vulnerable_example:
if user and user.password == request.form['password']:
    login(user)

categories.name: Software or Data Integrity Failures
categories.description: Renamed (and to 'or'). Missing integrity checks on code, updates and data, at a lower level than supply chain failures.
categories.fixed_example:
import json
obj = json.loads(request.data)  # data only, never executable objects

categories.name: Security Logging & Alerting Failures
categories.description: Renamed from Logging and Monitoring. Logging without alerting is of little use for catching incidents.

categories.name: Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions
categories.description: New in 2025. Poor error handling, logical errors and failing open when something unusual happens.

lists.status: Official release, now marked superseded by the 2025 list on the OWASP project page

categories.name: Broken Access Control
categories.description: Users can act outside their intended permissions: reading other users' data, changing records, or reaching admin functions.

categories.name: Cryptographic Failures
categories.description: Sensitive data is not protected in transit or at rest, or weak or misused cryptography is used.
categories.fixed_example:
import bcrypt
h = bcrypt.hashpw(password.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt())

categories.name: Injection
categories.description: Untrusted input is sent to an interpreter (SQL, OS shell, LDAP, browser) and runs as commands. Includes cross-site scripting.
categories.vulnerable_example: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'")
categories.fixed_example: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s", (name,))

categories.name: Insecure Design
categories.description: Missing or weak security controls in the design itself, such as no threat modeling or unsafe business flows. Not fixable by perfect code alone.

categories.name: Security Misconfiguration
categories.description: Insecure defaults, unneeded features, verbose errors, missing hardening, or misconfigured cloud services.
categories.fixed_example:
app.config['DEBUG'] = False
ADMIN_PASSWORD = os.environ['ADMIN_PASSWORD']

categories.name: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
categories.description: Using libraries, frameworks or other components with known vulnerabilities or that are no longer supported.
categories.fixed_example:
# requirements: pin a patched version and scan dependencies in CI
log4j-core==2.17.1

categories.name: Identification and Authentication Failures
categories.description: Weak login, credential, or session handling lets attackers assume other users' identities.
categories.vulnerable_example:
if user and user.password == request.form['password']:
    login(user)

categories.name: Software and Data Integrity Failures
categories.description: Code and data are trusted without integrity checks: unsafe deserialization, unsigned updates, insecure CI/CD pipelines.
categories.fixed_example:
import json
obj = json.loads(request.data)  # data only, never executable objects

categories.name: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
categories.description: Security events are not logged, monitored or alerted on, so attacks go unnoticed.

categories.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
categories.description: The server fetches a URL supplied by the user, letting attackers reach internal services or cloud metadata.
categories.fixed_example:
host = urlparse(url).hostname
if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS:
    abort(400)
return requests.get(url, timeout=5).text
